### The research question
EEG 表示中的哪些可预测信息，在更换试次、会话或被试后仍然成立？现有证据允许我们把这些信息解释到什么程度？

Priority: task info vs identity/environment info. How much of a high score depends on trial, subject, session, stimulus, recording conditions? Which tests distinguish? What survives change of trial/session/subject?

Extension choice: Group 2 (missing info vs limited readout). Rationale: the EEG-FM benchmark shows linear probing often nearly collapses to chance while full fine-tuning reaches well above chance on the same frozen features' source — that is a readout-capacity contrast, and it's the cheapest to test and most decision-relevant (whether to invest in representation learning vs. better probes/adaptation). Group 3 (pretraining objective structure) has weaker discriminating power because interventions (masking ratio, spectral target, channel masking) confound tokenization, receptive field, and augmentation simultaneously — I can say that and thus choose group 2.

### Literature map (8 items)
1. Chevallier et al. 2024, MOABB benchmark (arXiv 2404.15319, J. Neural Eng.) — evaluation taxonomy; within-session is upper bound; most literature uses it; cross-session/cross-subject is a transfer problem.
2. Yin et al. 2025 EMNLP — data leakage in cross-subject splitting inflates brain-to-text decoding.
3. Liu et al. 2026 (arXiv 2601.17883) — 12 FMs, 13 datasets, LOO cross-subject + within-subject few-shot, full FT vs linear probe: linear probing frequently insufficient; specialists competitive; larger models not necessarily better.
4. Jiang et al. 2024 LaBraM — masked codebook/spectrum prediction, 2500h pretraining, downstream TUAB/TUEV with patient-level splits (train/test separation provided by dataset; validation split at patient level). Note: no cross-subject LOO for its main claims; the "generalization" claim is cross-dataset not cross-subject.
5. Banville et al. 2021 — SSL on clinical EEG; embeddings encode sleep stage, pathology, age, gender, AND recording-site/date/channel-count clusters → i.e., environment/identity info is entangled in the representation. This is a crucial piece: the same embedding space carries clinical structure and acquisition nuisance.
6. Fallahi et al. 2026 — brainwave biometrics on 345 subjects/6007 sessions over 5 years: identity is decodable, EER increases from 6.7% (1 day) to 14.3% (1 year); session/device clusters dominate embedding space. → identity survives session change only partially, and environment info is strong.
7. Hebart & Baker 2018 — decoding ≠ representation; predictive voxels can be in ventricles (physiological noise); prediction vs interpretation.
8. EEGManyPipelines (couldn't fetch — mention as unresolved/not cited? I can cite only fetched. I'll note it as a lead not verified → mention in "what is missing" without citing as evidence, being explicit it's unverified.)

- Also could add a paper on "EEG decoding within-session vs cross-session motor imagery" from MOABB original (Jayaram & Barachant 2018) — but MOABB 2024 covers.
